flashcards.back: The first place after the decimal point: the whole split into ten equal parts, so each part is one tenth and 0.4 is four tenths.
The second place after the decimal point: the whole split into one hundred tiny parts, so 0.25 is twenty-five hundredths.
What a digit is worth because of where it stands: the same 4 is worth four tenths in 0.4 and would be worth four hundredths in 0.04.
The dot that separates the wholes from the tenths: everything to its right is less than one whole.

flashcards.front: Comparing decimals by digit count: 0.25 looks bigger than 0.4 because 25 > 4.
flashcards.back: Longer digit strings feel larger, but place value decides, not digit count. Match the place values first: 0.4 is 0.40, then tenths under tenths and hundredths under hundredths. In the animation scene s4 the tenths bar and the hundredths square are laid over the same whole, and 0.4 visibly covers more: never judge a decimal by how many digits it has.

items.prompt: How many hundredths are in 0.25? Split your answer into tenths and hundredths.
Explain why ten hundredths is the same as one tenth.
items.answer: The whole split into hundredths has ten tiny parts in each tenth column, so ten hundredths fill exactly one tenth.
